headline.claim_origin: AR-VERIFY raw/compute_ar_verify.py:415 = v_bus(400) + v_line_peak(186.676); an explicit sum of two node potentials.
headline.why_not: No board node is the series sum of the bus and the line peak. On a boost-switch short the bus is isolated from the bridge by the reverse-biased boost diode, and the bridge sees only the line. On a boost-diode short the bus is placed on the bridge output, but the bridge's own low-side diode clamps each AC terminal, so a bridge device blocks at most ~V_bus (400 V), not V_bus+V_line.
headline.is_there_any_real_586_7_path: No. The bridge's own upper/lower devices clamp every AC terminal between MINUS and PLUS, so no AC node can sit V_bus+V_line from the opposite rail; the largest device span is ~V_bus (400 V, diode-short case). 586.7 V is a sum of two node potentials that never appear in series across a device on this board (a bridgeless/totem-pole stage would be needed for that).

boost_switch_short.bridge_device_v: line peak 186.676 V across the AC terminals; output tracks the rectified line

boost_diode_short.note: the bus IS placed on the bridge output, but a bridge diode sees ~V_bus, not V_bus+V_line

compound_fault.note: no real node: the bridge clamps prevent V_bus+V_line (see inputs.json fault_paths.C)

bus_capacitance_and_energy.where_it_discharges: A bare boost-switch short does NOT discharge the bank: U10 blocks it. It discharges through the passive bleeders (tau 672 s) or an external load. On a boost-diode short with U9 conducting it discharges through U9+shunt (tau ~116 us, 179 J).

interruption.fuse: F1 Schurter 0034.3129 FST 5x20mm, 16 A / 250 V time-lag (holder U2 0031.2510)
interruption.line_fed_switch_short_interrupted_by_fus: YES in principle; clearing time not established (pre-arcing I2t not captured)
interruption.line_vs_cap_distinction: line-fed current is bounded by source impedance and cleared by F1; cap discharge is an internal loop F1 cannot see.

answers.mov_statement: U7 V150LA10AP is line-to-neutral (l1 to AC_N). Neither bus rail reaches it. No MOV clamp figure was used in this assessment.

recommendations.bridge_device_required_voltage_class: 600 V is adequate for the single-fault blocking case (~400 V, 1.5x); the 586.7 V claim does not force 800/1000 V. On the actual board U1 is already 1000 V.
recommendations.switch_current_energy_withstand: The switch-short stress is current/energy. The surviving bridge must be protected inside IFSM 350 A / I2t 510 A2s.
recommendations.protection_addition: Coordinate F1's I2t with the fault current; add bus-side protection (fuse/crowbar/fast controller shutdown) for the internal cap-discharge loop; resolve the line impedance.

unresolved_assumptions: NTC bypass state at the fault instant.
C3D20065D surge rating; LGX datasheet not independently captured.
Bus setpoint tolerance/overshoot; external load at fault.
single_most_important_missing_input: The AC source/line impedance at the fault (with the parallel need for F1's pre-arcing I2t): the line impedance sets the prospective fault current, and the fuse I2t sets whether it is cleared before the bridge (IFSM 350 A / I2t 510 A2s) is destroyed.
